To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TPA approach can be used to quantitate the expression levels of multiple hepatic uptake transport proteins in human liver tissue samples with a high degree of accuracy.

the total protein approach (TPA)-based quantification of hepatic transporters showed good-to-excessive correlation (Pearson r=0.74-1.00) with the targeted data and the values were similar with 71% of the TPA values within 3-fold range of the targeted data.
global proteomic experiments are able to detect differences in transporter expression and can estimate transporter expression levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of global proteomic approaches to quantitate hepatic drug transporter expression in human liver tissue.
the development of a novel method for the detection of protein expression levels in a large number of protein samples.
the use of global proteomic data to provide quantitative protein information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

multiplexed global quantitation is a useful approach for the initial assessment of protein expression levels and that the data can be further validated using targeted proteomic assays for a subset of the proteins.
multiplexed global quantitative proteomics provides an alternative approach to targeted proteomic assays and is suitable for the quantification of drug transporters in tissue samples.
the TPA-based global proteomic quantitation of drug transporter proteins can be considered as a valuable and cost-effective alternative to targeted quantitation for a limited number of transporters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the TPA-based approach can provide a good estimation of protein abundances, which may be useful in situations where a limited number of targeted assays are available.
the TPA-based global proteomic data are a good surrogate for the targeted data, and the TPA approach is a viable alternative to targeted proteomics for protein quantification in biological matrices.
multiplexed global quantitative proteomic experiments are capable of providing protein abundance information that can be used to compare samples and estimate protein abundances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
global proteomics can be a powerful tool to provide a broad assessment of the relative protein expression levels of a large number of proteins.
multiplexed global quantitation can be used as an alternative to targeted quantification, especially when the targeted approach is not feasible or is cost-prohibitive.

the TPA is an efficient approach to quantify large numbers of proteins in a single experiment, which can provide a reasonable estimation of protein expression levels and can be used for relative quantitation between samples.
